title: Midnight in Rotterdam
description: A shipment created near midnight UTC can land on a different calendar day (or even a different month) depending on which timezone the report is viewed in. Prove the day-bucketing is timezone-aware, not hardcoded to UTC.
successCondition: Set a shipment's createdAt directly in the database to 2026-01-01T23:30:00.000Z (a value chosen to sit right at a day boundary in some timezones but not others). GET /api/reporting/summary?groupBy=day&timeZone=UTC buckets it under period "2026-01-01", while the same query with timeZone=Pacific/Kiritimati (UTC+14) buckets it under "2026-01-02" — the same shipment, two different day buckets, purely from the timezone parameter.
hints: This one needs direct DB access to set up a deterministic fixture — `npm run db:psql` (see docs/self-host.md) or any Postgres client works against the local dev database.
timeZone accepts any IANA zone name — Node's Intl API resolves it, no timezone database setup required on your end.
